messages:
Maya (marketing): Hey team — we need signoff on the numbers for the press claim. Can runtime confirm the final latency/cost samples and the raw payloads we can attach to the press kit?
Omar (runtime): Yes. We can produce raw single-run artifacts + aggregated percentiles. What exact artifacts do you want in the press pack? csv/json?
Maya (marketing): CSV preferred for downstream analysts. Need P50/P95/P99, sample payloads (10 small, 10 medium, 10 long), and the exact run command + env so the press/legal folks can reproduce if asked. Also callouts for quantized vs fp16 differences.
Jules (eng-runtime): We can do that. Want to confirm methodology: warmup tokens, request distribution (mix of seq lengths), batching config, and model variant names. If you want deterministic runs, we'll lock seeds and disable autoscaling.
Maya (marketing): Exactly. We need a short plain-language description of methodology for the release notes too. One-paragraph. No heavy jargon.
Omar (runtime): Plan: 1) deterministic single-worker runs for per-token latency; 2) 3 trial runs per payload then median; 3) warmup 50 requests; 4) batching set to none for 95th percentile sim (min-batch=1); 5) provide quantized (q4_0) and fp16 outputs.
Lena (data-ops): I'll produce the CSV with columns: payload_id, seq_len, model_variant, quantization, trial_n, lat_ms, tokens, p50_over_trials, p95_over_trials, notes. Also attach a README.md explaining provenance and the exact docker image hash.
Maya (marketing): Nice. Can you include a small sample CSV row for the press reviewers? They sometimes ask to see the raw row structure.
Jules (eng-runtime): Yep. Sample row: `payload_03,256,redwood-v1.2.0,q4_0,2,12.4,256,12.1,13.2,quantized-with-warmup`
Omar (runtime): For reproducible command, use this (we'll include as-is in README):
```
# runbench.sh
./run_bench --model redwood-v1.2.0 --seq 256 --quant q4_0 --warmup 50 --trials 3 --batching off --seed 1337 --out results.csv
```
Maya (marketing): Perfect. Two quick asks: 1) can you run an extra cold-start sweep (no warmup) for 100 short requests and include a heatmap image? 2) Can you annotate any runs where the warmup cache materially changed P95 (>10% change)?
Omar (runtime): We can do both. Cold-start sweep will be a separate artifact folder. We'll generate a 2D heatmap png with request index vs lat_ms. Annotation: we'll add a column `warmup_effect` where value is `yes` if P95 delta >10%.
Lena (data-ops): We'll also checksum all artifacts and put them in a signed tarball with the docker image digest. I'll drop the tarball link here when ready.
Maya (marketing): ETA? We want to lock the press text tomorrow EOD.
Jules (eng-runtime): Can get the CSV, README, and sample payloads by EOD tomorrow if nothing else blocks. Cold-start heatmap might be +6 hours after that.
Omar (runtime): Scheduling bench runs now. Posting a short bot update when the first artifacts land.
bench-bot: run queued: bench-20260312-001 (redwood-v1.2.0), ETA 18m.
Maya (marketing): Awesome, thanks. Please @ me when the tarball is up — I need the direct link for the press agent. :thumbsup:
Omar (runtime): Will do. If legal asks for dataset privacy notes, we used synthetic and redacted PII where needed; I'll include that note in the README.
Maya (marketing): Great. No embargo issues on this one. Thanks all!
